title: Hawk: Harnessing Hardware-Aware Knowledge for High-Performance NPU Kernel Generation
event_hint: Hawk: a training-free framework that uses hardware-aware knowledge (run-time synthesis, 2D retrieval, effect-driven distillation) to let LLMs generate high-performance Ascend NPU (Ascend C) kernels, targeting the Ascend Da Vinci architecture.
problem: Generating high-performance NPU kernels with LLMs fails because LLMs lack hardware-specific priors: state-of-the-art LLMs achieve only 13.3% Comp@1 and 13.3% Pass@1 on Ascend C (vs 100%/80% on CUDA), over 75% of failures stem from low-level hardware-specific misuses, and even correct NPU kernels run ~20x slower than GPU equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.
mechanism: Hawk is a training-free framework with three modules. (1) Run-Time Knowledge Synthesis uses a Triple-Part Executable Knowledge Representation (indexing triggers, semantic rationales, exact syntactic templates) to couple error context with executable semantics, captured dynamically at run time. (2) Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval uses a 2D-Retrieval paradigm projecting queries into a syntactic space (API signature compliance) and a hardware-aligned semantic space (memory/parallelization constraints). (3) Effect-Driven Knowledge Distillation uses LLM-driven semantic arbitration with physical NPU compilation/execution feedback to prune erroneous and redundant knowledge entries. Targets the Ascend Da Vinci architecture (AI Cube, AI Vector, multi-tier memory with MTE engines, explicit instruction pipelining).

evidence.claim: Hawk elevates NPU kernel generation accuracy from 49.4% to 80.0% and achieves up to 2.2x execution speedup over state-of-the-art baselines on real-world Ascend NPU workloads.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract; PDF Page 11 - Conclusion

evidence.claim: SOTA LLMs achieve only 13.3% Comp@1 and 13.3% Pass@1 on Ascend C, vs 100.0% Comp@1 and up to 86.7% Pass@1 on CUDA (DeepSeek-V4 Pro and GLM-4.5, 15 activation kernels from MultiKernelBench, add-shot prompting).
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GLM-4.5; 15 activation kernels; MultiKernelBench
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 3 - Table I

evidence.claim: Of 126 classified Ascend C generation failures, 98 (77.8%) are syntax-level (including 53 runtime timeouts, 27 non-existent functions) and 26 (20.6%) are hardware-level (UB overflow); only 2 (1.6%) are numeric correctness mismatches.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 3 - Table II

evidence.claim: Even functionally correct Ascend C kernels execute nearly 20x slower than their GPU equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.

Sample timing on RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2 shows Ascend C kernels far slower than CUDA (e.g., diagonal op: CUDA 0.2ms vs Ascend 37.4ms, 295.6x normalized slowdown; ~22x slower vs PyTorch NPU baseline).
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 5 - Table IV

evaluation_context: Evaluated on real-world Ascend NPU workloads (Ascend C kernels). LLMs tested: DeepSeek-V4 Pro and GLM-4.5 (plus supplementary DeepSeek-V4-Flash). Hardware platforms: RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2. Benchmark: MultiKernelBench, 15 activation kernels (L1/L2 coverage). Knowledge base covers 431 kernels across 8 development-paradigm dimensions. Baselines include fine-tuning (AscendKernelGen, EvoKernel) and IR-assisted frameworks (AKG, AscendCraft, STARK, CudaForge, AVO).
limitations: Test suite covers L1 and L2 kernels; scaling to highly complex fused operators on advanced NPU clusters is left as future work. The 49.4% baseline-accuracy figure is stated without specifying which baseline framework produced it in the visible evidence. Speedup is reported as 'up to 2.2x' (best case); distribution across operator types is not fully exposed. Generalization beyond Ascend (Da Vinci/CANN) is claimed for Ascend 310/950 but not separately measured in the visible evidence.
project_relevance: Hawk is a software/compiler-tooling contribution (NPU kernel generation via LLM + hardware-aware knowledge) rather than a new chip architecture; it is relevant to HW/SW codesign and the memory-IO codesign direction because it targets the Ascend memory hierarchy (Unified Buffer, L0/L1, MTE engines) and exposes how implicit hardware constraints dominate kernel performance. For the project card it addresses the software side of converting NPU peak compute into real throughput, not a silicon or packaging change.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.01590v2 (2 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from Sun Yat-sen University, GBA National Tech Innovation Center, Peng Cheng Laboratory.
Targets Ascend NPU (Da Vinci architecture, CANN toolchain); hardware platforms RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2.
The 49.4% baseline and 80.0% Hawk accuracy are consistently reported; the specific SOTA baseline behind 49.4% is not named in the visible evidence.
